newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: PRESS DIGEST - CZECH REPUBLIC - OCT 29.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - CZECH REPUBLIC - OCT 29.

text.p: HOSPODARSKE NOVINY - Czech exports to Slovakia exceeded imports by 9.1 billion crowns in the first nine months of 1996. Slovakia is The Czech Republic's second largest trading partner.

- The sixth annual Invex computer trade fair in Brno saw sales of approximately 2.5 billion crowns. Invex, which has become one of the three largest computer trade fairs in Europe, saw 1,034 firms from 17 countries take part.
- Brno Broker Group has opened "Czech Fund", the first Czech open investment fund in Canada.
- Aral Czech Republic a.s., the largest foreign owner of filling stations on the Czech market, expects sales to reach 3.5 billion crowns this year.

- Jihoceska Plynarenska will obtain natural gas from Germany starting in 2003. There will be a pipeline between Freyung on the German side and Lenora in the Czech Republic. MLADA FRONTA DNES - The National Property Fund will sell 45 percent of Uniplet Trebic in a public tender. The orientation price is 132.2 million crowns.

- Miroslav Macek, an official at the Health Ministry has been criticised by the Civic Democratic Party (ODS) because of his recently released plan for reforms in healthcare. The criticism did not center on the plan itself, but on the fact that Macek did not confer with the party or with the Minister of Health. PRAVO - Chemapol Group has decided to increase its basic capital from between 500 million crowns to 1.64 billion crowns through the sales of new shares. The final amount will be decided upon by the end of the year by the board of directors.
- Each one percent tranche of Vitkovice a.s. which the National Property Fund is to sell to Rafis Trading Ostrava by the end of the year, should cost between 25 and 30 million crowns.
